what: Nicaraguan indigenous leader dies after three years in prison

clean_source_blocks.text: Rights groups condemn the death of Brooklyn Rivera, 73, following his long arbitrary detention by the governing regime.

Dánica Coto, Associated Press Dánica Coto, Associated Press SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) — Brooklyn Rivera, a renowned Indigenous leader from Nicaragua who spent years fighting for the rights of his community and was imprisoned by the government in September 2023, has died. The Nicaraguan government issued a statement Sunday saying that Rivera died from a bacterial infection after his health had declined following a case of COVID-19, which led to his physical and neurological deterioration. Human rights activists and groups worldwide denounced his death and a previous statement by the government in which they referred to Rivera as "Brother" and said they were praying for him.

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) — Brooklyn Rivera, a renowned Indigenous leader from Nicaragua who spent years fighting for the rights of his community and was imprisoned by the government in September 2023, has died. The Nicaraguan government issued a statement Sunday claiming that Rivera died from a bacterial infection after his health had declined following a case of COVID-19, which led to his physical and neurological deterioration. Human rights activists and groups worldwide denounced his death and a statement that the government released Saturday in which they referred to Rivera as “Brother” and said they were praying for him.

A leading Nicaraguan indigenous leader has died after being detained by the ruling authoritarian regime for nearly three years. Brooklyn Rivera, who founded the central American nation's indigenous movement Yatama, died due to "physical and neurological deterioration" linked to a Covid-19 infection, the Nicaraguan Ministry of Health stated on Sunday. The government, headed by President Daniel Ortega, took 15 hours to confirm the death and are refusing to release the 73-year-old's body to his family, opposition media report. The Nicaraguan government is routinely accused of political oppression, and Rivera is one of a growing number of dissidents to die in custody. Rivera had been arbitrarily detained when he returned to his home in Nicaragua in September 2023.

[Lähde: BBC World]
A leading Nicaraguan indigenous leader has died after being detained by the ruling authoritarian regime for nearly three years.

Brooklyn Rivera, who founded the central American nation's indigenous movement Yatama, died due to "physical and neurological deterioration" linked to a Covid-19 infection, the Nicaraguan Ministry of Health stated on Sunday.

The government, headed by President Daniel Ortega, took 15 hours to confirm the death and are refusing to release the 73-year-old's body to his family, opposition media report.

The Nicaraguan government is routinely accused of political oppression, and Rivera is one of a growing number of dissidents to die in custody.

Rivera had been arbitrarily detained when he returned to his home in Nicaragua in September 2023.

He had long fought for indigenous autonomy in Nicaragua, and had opposed Ortega's Sandinista revolutionary government in the 1980s as part of an indigenous militia that fought alongside the Contras.

Rivera's detainment was only recognised by the regime more than a year after it began, following pressure from other nations.

Little was heard of his condition until Wednesday, when the government acknowledged he had been in hospital in the capital, Managua, since early March.

It said he had been suffering from a range of conditions including "cerebral edema associated with severe neurological injury", a respiratory infection and renal failure.

Nicaragua's Ministry of Health released an image of an emaciated Rivera lying in a hospital bed being ventilated via a tube through his neck.

News of his ill health sparked renewed calls for his release.

The US State Department said Rivera had been "unjustly imprisoned", and the Nicaraguan Ministry of Health's statement was "an attempt to conceal its central role in the cruel treatment and Rivera's current conditions".

"This repression, violence and lack of humanity is abominable," it added.

Meanwhile, César Marín, Amnesty International spokesperson for the region, said: "Brooklyn Rivera must be released immediately and unconditionally.

"His critical health condition while in the custody of the Nicaraguan state confirms the extreme risk to which he has been exposed."

The Nicaraguan Ministry of Health said on Sunday that Rivera had been surrounded by several members of his family when he died.

It had earlier said he could not be transferred elsewhere due to his degenerating condition.

News of Rivera's death was met by condemnation.

payload.title: Nicaragualainen alkuperäiskansojen johtaja Brooklyn Rivera on kuollut vankeuden jälkeen
payload.summary: Nicaragualainen alkuperäiskansojen oikeuksien puolustaja Brooklyn Rivera on kuollut 73-vuotiaana oltuaan vangittuna syyskuusta 2023 lähtien. Ihmisoikeustoimijat ovat tuominneet hänen kuolemansa ja aiemman mielivaltaiseksi kuvatun pidätyksensä.
payload.content:
Nicaragualainen alkuperäiskansojen johtaja Brooklyn Rivera on kuollut 73-vuotiaana oltuaan vangittuna syyskuusta 2023 lähtien. Rivera tunnettiin Yatama-liikkeen perustajana ja pitkäaikaisena alkuperäiskansojen oikeuksien puolustajana. Nicaraguan viranomaisten mukaan hänen kuolemansa liittyi bakteeri-infektioon ja covid-19-taudin jälkeiseen fyysiseen ja neurologiseen heikkenemiseen. Ihmisoikeusjärjestöt ja -toimijat ovat tuominneet sekä Riveran kuoleman että hänen pitkän vankeutensa.

## Pitkä ura alkuperäiskansojen puolustajana

Riveraa kuvataan merkittäväksi nicaragualaiseksi alkuperäiskansojen johtajaksi, joka käytti vuosia yhteisönsä oikeuksien ajamiseen. Hän perusti Yataman, Nicaraguan alkuperäiskansojen liikkeen, ja nousi tunnetuksi poliittiseksi hahmoksi maassa, jossa hallintoa on toistuvasti syytetty poliittisesta sorrosta.

Rivera vangittiin sen jälkeen, kun hän palasi kotiinsa Nicaraguaan syyskuussa 2023. Hänen pidätystään on kuvattu mielivaltaiseksi. Kuolema on herättänyt kansainvälistä arvostelua erityisesti siksi, että hän oli pitkään hallinnon hallussa ja yksi useista toisinajattelijoista, joiden on kerrottu kuolleen vankeudessa.

## Viranomaiset kertoivat terveydentilan heikentyneen

Nicaraguan terveysministeriö ilmoitti sunnuntaina, että Rivera kuoli bakteeri-infektioon sen jälkeen, kun hänen terveytensä oli heikentynyt covid-19-taudin seurauksena. Viranomaisten mukaan sairaus johti fyysiseen ja neurologiseen rappeutumiseen.

Oppositiomedia on kertonut, että presidentti Daniel Ortegan johtama hallinto vahvisti kuoleman vasta 15 tunnin kuluttua ja että Riveran ruumista ei ole luovutettu hänen perheelleen. Nämä tiedot ovat osa tapausta koskevaa arvostelua, jota on kohdistettu Ortegan hallintoon ja sen tapaan kohdella hallinnon vastustajiksi nähtyjä henkilöitä.

## Kritiikki kohdistuu myös hallituksen viestintään

Ihmisoikeustoimijat ovat arvostelleet myös hallituksen aiempaa lausuntoa, jossa Riveraasta käytettiin veljeen viittaavaa ilmaisua ja kerrottiin viranomaisten rukoilevan hänen puolestaan. Arvostelijoiden mukaan lausunto oli ristiriidassa sen kanssa, että Rivera oli ollut pitkään hallinnon pidättämänä.

Riveran kuolema lisää huomiota Nicaraguan poliittiseen tilanteeseen ja hallinnon kohteluun toisinajattelijoita sekä alkuperäiskansojen oikeuksien puolustajia kohtaan. Lähdeaineiston perusteella seuraava keskeinen kysymys on, luovutetaanko hänen ruumiinsa perheelle ja miten viranomaiset vastaavat kuolemaa koskevaan kansainväliseen kritiikkiin.
summary_bullets: Brooklyn Rivera kuoli 73-vuotiaana oltuaan vangittuna syyskuusta 2023 lähtien.
Nicaraguan viranomaiset sanoivat kuoleman liittyneen bakteeri-infektioon ja covid-19-taudin jälkeiseen terveydentilan heikkenemiseen.
Ihmisoikeustoimijat ovat tuominneet Riveran kuoleman ja hänen aiemman pidätyksensä.
payload.journalist_note: Aineisto tukee ydintietoja Riveran kuolemasta, vankeudesta, viranomaisten ilmoittamasta kuolinsyystä ja ihmisoikeustoimijoiden kritiikistä. Oppositiomedian väitteet ruumiin luovuttamatta jättämisestä ja kuoleman vahvistamisen viiveestä on esitetty lähdeaineiston mukaisesti.

SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) — Brooklyn Rivera, a renowned Indigenous leader from Nicaragua who spent years fighting for the rights of his community and was imprisoned by the government in September 2023, has died. The Nicaraguan government issued a statement Sunday claiming that Rivera died from a bacterial infection after his health had declined following a case of COVID-19, which led to his physical and neurological deterioration. Human rights activists and groups worldwide denounced his death and a statement that the government released Saturday in which they referred to Rivera as “Brother” and said they were praying for him.

A leading Nicaraguan indigenous leader has died after being detained by the ruling authoritarian regime for nearly three years. Brooklyn Rivera, who founded the central American nation's indigenous movement Yatama, died due to "physical and neurological deterioration" linked to a Covid-19 infection, the Nicaraguan Ministry of Health stated on Sunday. The government, headed by President Daniel Ortega, took 15 hours to confirm the death and are refusing to release the 73-year-old's body to his family, opposition media report. The Nicaraguan government is routinely accused of political oppression, and Rivera is one of a growing number of dissidents to die in custody. Rivera had been arbitrarily detained when he returned to his home in Nicaragua in September 2023.
